reserveReview.reviewer: GLM issue-sweep 2026-09-29 (WithheldFallbackCircle) — fallback-composition reconciliation to the Deloitte July 2026 examination (report PDF read directly this pass)
reserveReview.rationale: Rows keep the live Circle transparency adapter's four slice identities (adapter-owned source keys) so V9 keeps classifying live rows, with weights reconciled to the Deloitte examination as of July 31, 2026 (read directly this pass: $71,904,101,332 fair value of USDC reserve assets vs $71,826,453,410 USDC in circulation). Mapping: <3-Month U.S. Treasuries $7,678,498,751 (Circle Reserve Fund U.S. Treasury securities $7,179,080,057, longest maturity 2026-10-15, plus other reserve Treasury securities $499,418,694) = 10.6788%; Overnight Reverse Treasury Repo $52,723,000,000 (report footnote 3: overnight lending to global financial institutions overcollateralized by U.S. Treasuries) = 73.3241%; the two deposit slices carry the examined net cash of $11,502,602,581 (fund cash $1,003,971,911 + cash at regulated financial institutions $10,607,410,596 + settlement/timing net -$108,779,926) = 15.9971%. The examination does not split cash between systemically important and other institutions; the split applies the Aug 06, 2026 weekly-disclosure deposit mix (47.4% SIFI / 52.6% other, from the previously curated $8.99B/$9.97B figures) to the July 31 examined net cash — both slices share the identical bank-deposit classification, so the split does not alter the risk picture. compositionAsOf equals the examination period end, so the curated rows are now the independently examined fallback composition; the 2026-08-08 pass deliberately omitted the date because its weights tracked the rolling weekly disclosure rather than the examined balance sheet.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Circle's 2025 Form 10-K states approximately 88% of USDC reserves sat in the BlackRock-managed Circle Reserve Fund (SEC-registered 2a-7 government money market fund) whose assets are held in the custody of BNY as of 2025-12-31; the remainder is cash at global banks, primarily systemically important institutions, whose individual names and shares are undisclosed. The 10-K states reserves are held in accounts titled FBO holders of USDC and that Circle does not lend, borrow against, or encumber the reserves, with applicable state regimes prohibiting lending, pledging, rehypothecating, or otherwise encumbering them. The same filing cautions that no court has ruled on stablecoin reserve treatment in an issuer bankruptcy, so bankruptcy remoteness stays contractual-only; custodian-failure replacement terms remain undisclosed.
